# Lus

> A small, fast, and productive language to build programs. Lus derives from Lua 5.5. One executable of about 7 MB runs scripts and carries a test runner, formatter, checker, documentation generator, debugger, and bundler. The standard library covers JSON, CSV, SQLite, HTTP clients and servers, TCP, UDP, TLS, compression, cryptography, time zones, and threads. Every script runs with no permissions until it pledges the ones it needs.

Agents writing Lus should install the `lus` skill below, then work in a loop of `lus check --json`, `lus fmt --write`, and `lus test --json`. Lus differs from Lua in a few places that matter for generated code: `catch` replaces `pcall`, strings are text indexed by character, raw bytes are vectors, and I/O functions raise an error until the script calls `pledge`. Each link below is a Markdown page.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://lus.dev/manual/getting-started.md): Install the binary and run a first program.
- [Lus for Lua programmers](https://lus.dev/manual/lua.md): What changes when porting from Lua 5.5, each Lua idiom beside its Lus form, and how `lus check` finds them.
- [Guide](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md): The language taught in order, from values to internals, in one page.
- [CLI](https://lus.dev/manual/cli.md): Every `lus` command and option.

## Agent skills

- [lus](https://lus.dev/agents/skills/lus/SKILL.md): Write, check, format, and test Lus code.
- [lus-rewrite](https://lus.dev/agents/skills/lus-rewrite/SKILL.md): Assess a project for Lus, preview it, and port it behind a parity harness.
- [lus-writing](https://lus.dev/agents/skills/lus-writing/SKILL.md): Write documentation, READMEs, and doc comments in the Lus prose style.
- [Install the skills](https://lus.dev/agents.md): `claude plugin install lus --marketplace lus-lang/lus` in Claude Code, `lus agents init` in any other agent.

## Standard library

- [API reference](https://lus.dev/manual/api.md): Every function, with parameters, return values, required permissions, and stability.
- [Permissions](https://lus.dev/manual/permissions.md): `pledge`, permission names and values, and `seal`.
- [Data formats](https://lus.dev/manual/data.md): JSON with filters and exact numbers, CSV, and the table and string extensions for data processing.
- [SQLite](https://lus.dev/manual/sqlite.md): `io.sqlite`, prepared statements, and transactions. Unstable.
- [Network](https://lus.dev/manual/network.md): `network.fetch`, TCP, UDP with bounded receives, and the `network.serve` HTTP server.
- [Coroutines and workers](https://lus.dev/manual/concurrency.md): `coroutine.detach`, and interpreter states on their own threads with message passing.
- [Filesystem](https://lus.dev/manual/filesystem.md): The `fs` library and `fs.path`.
- [Time](https://lus.dev/manual/time.md): Instants, durations, and zoned times with embedded tzdata. Unstable.
- [Cryptography](https://lus.dev/manual/crypto.md): SHA-2 digests, HMAC, Ed25519 signatures, Argon2id password hashes, secure random bytes, UUIDs, and ULIDs. Unstable.
- [Text and bytes](https://lus.dev/manual/text.md): WTF-8 strings measured in characters, vectors for binary data, transcoding, and compression through `vector.archive`.

## Language

- [Guide](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md): The language taught in order, with the standard library and the internals.
- [Lus for Lua programmers](https://lus.dev/manual/lua.md): Porting from Lua, and the Lus form of each Lua idiom.
- [Lus and other runtimes](https://lus.dev/manual/runtimes.md): Benchmark results against six other runtimes, and the design choices behind them.
- [Best practices](https://lus.dev/manual/practices.md): File layout, permissions, errors, concurrency, testing, and performance habits.
- [Catch](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#catching-errors) and [catch handlers](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#catch-handlers): Expression-level error handling.
- [Optional chaining](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#optional-chaining): The `?` suffix operator.
- [Conditions that declare variables](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#conditions-that-declare-variables): `if x = f() then` and `while line = read() do`.
- [Destructuring](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#destructuring-with-from) and [destructuring loops](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#destructuring-each-item-with-from): `local a, b from t` and `for a, b from iter do`.
- [String interpolation](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#strings): Backtick strings with `$name` and `$(expr)`.
- [Do expressions](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#do-expressions): Blocks that `provide` a value.
- [Enums](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#enums), [slices](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#slices), [runtime attributes](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#runtime-attributes), and [local groups](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#local-groups).
- [Continue](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#break-and-continue): Skip to the next iteration of a loop.
- [Build flags](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#build-flags) and [values computed when the file is compiled](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#values-computed-when-the-file-is-compiled): `-F` flags, `if` branches that the compiler removes, and `<meta>` locals.
- [Values computed on first use](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#values-computed-on-first-use): `<lazy>` locals and group fields, and `<lazy, close>`.
- [Values that follow other values](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#values-that-follow-other-values): `<observe>` locals that recompute when the locals they name are assigned.
- [Values for each coroutine](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#values-for-each-coroutine): `<context>` locals, which hold one value per coroutine, and `debug.getcontext`.
- [Bigints and decimals](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#numbers): `123n` and `1.50d`.
- [Queries](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#queries): First-class queries over tables and databases. Unstable.

## Tools

- [Testing](https://lus.dev/manual/testing.md): `lus test`, case tables, power asserts, and snapshots.
- [Developer tools](https://lus.dev/manual/tools.md): `lus fmt`, `lus check`, `lus doc`, `lus ast`, `lus build`, and `lus compile`.
- [Standalone binaries](https://lus.dev/manual/tools.md#standalone-executables): One executable with the script, its modules, and its permissions.
- [Faster forms](https://lus.dev/manual/tools.md#faster-forms): The `lus check` hints that name a measured faster form of correct code, and the [diagnostic codes](https://lus.dev/manual/tools.md#diagnostic-codes) with their severities.
- [Debugger](https://lus.dev/manual/tools.md#debugger): `lus debug` over the Debug Adapter Protocol.

## Optional

- [Full documentation](https://lus.dev/llms-full.txt): The guide, the topic pages, and the API reference in one file.
- [Compact documentation](https://lus.dev/llms-small.txt): The language differences and every function signature, sized for a small context.
- [Embedding API](https://lus.dev/manual/embedding.md): The `lus.h` C interface for host programs.
- [WebAssembly](https://lus.dev/manual/webassembly.md): The runtime as a WASI module with a JavaScript host.
- [Build flags](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#build-flags), [preinclusion](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#preincluded-modules), and [readonly environment](https://lus.dev/manual/guide.md#the---readonly-env-option): Build and startup options.
- [Benchmarks](https://lus.dev/benchmarks.md): Lus against Node.js, Bun, Python, Ruby, PHP, and Lua on six programs, with the method.
